summary: Payment failures are caused by disk exhaustion on the SHARED ledger-db postgres, not by payment-service v6.0.0. ledger-db's disk grew from ~78% (11:00) to 100% (~15:02) because an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retained tens of GB of WAL; once full, all ledger-db writers failed with 'No space left on device', collapsing payment success from ~99% to ~35% at 15:00. The v6.0.0 deploy (14:46) and its rollback (15:12) are coincidental: errors persisted unchanged after rollback, and order-service (unrelated code) failed identically at 15:00:42. Remedy is to drop/fix the inactive replication slot and free disk, not to chase the release.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db disk exhaustion from inactive replication slot retaining WAL
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' on the shared postgres ledger-db retained tens of GB of WAL, growing the data volume from ~78% at 11:00 to 100% by ~15:02. Once the disk was full, all writers to ledger-db (payment-service ledger writes, order-service inserts) failed with 'No space left on device', causing the observed ~61% payment error rate and low payment success rate. The payment-service v6.0.0 deploy/rollback is coincidental.

causal_chain.claim: CDC consumer disconnects, leaving replication slot 'analytics_cdc' inactive
Postgres retains WAL for the stale slot (33-92 GB), growing the data volume toward full
ledger-db write/extension fails with 'No space left on device'
payment-service ledger writes fail -> ~61% error rate; order-service inserts also fail

assumptions: The 'analytics_cdc' slot is genuinely inactive (consumer/CDC pipeline down) and not merely slow
No other workload contributed materially to disk growth

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 introduced a faulty ledger write path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v6.0.0 mandate flow's new MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type caused ledger write failures, producing the payment errors. This is the reporter's hypothesis.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by: (a) error message is a storage-space error, not a schema/code error; (b) errors persisted at ~61-64% after the 15:12 rollback (F11); (c) unrelated order-service failed identically at 15:00:42 (F7); (d) disk was already 90%+ before the 14:46 deploy (F4).

assumptions: The 'analytics_cdc' replication slot's consumer is genuinely offline/inactive rather than merely lagging.
No other workload (e.g., an unindexed report query) contributed materially to the disk growth; the WAL retention is the dominant factor.
The metric 'disk_used_pct' for ledger-db reflects the same filesystem (/var/lib/postgresql/data) referenced in the disk-usage warnings.

timeline.event: ledger-db disk already at 78.23% and climbing
ledger-db warns replication slot 'analytics_cdc' inactive, retaining 63157 MB WAL
payment-service v6.0.0 deployed (new UPI mandate flow)
payment-service first 'No space left on device' ledger write errors; error rate jumps to 61%
order-service also begins failing INSERTs with 'No space left on device'
ledger-db PANIC/could not write pg_wal and base files
payment-service v6.0.0 rolled back; error rate unchanged (~62%) afterwards
payment error rate still 61.63%, disk still 100%

recommended_actions.action: Drop the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' (after confirming the CDC/analytics consumer is truly dead) and reclaim WAL to free ledger-db disk.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the direct driver of disk growth; HIST-114 was resolved the same way.

recommended_actions.action: Add a slot-lag/inactive-slot alert and a disk-capacity alert on ledger-db (and free space if needed via WAL archival).
recommended_actions.rationale: Detectting inactive slots earlier would have prevented a 4-hour runway to full disk.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT continue treating v6.0.0 as the culprit; verify recovery by monitoring disk_used_pct and payment error after slot removal.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback did not fix the symptom; further code churn wastes recovery time.

recommended_actions.action: Audit monitor/reporting pipelines that own replication slots to keep them connected or auto-drop stale slots.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of the same resource-exhaustion mechanism.

data_gaps: ledger-db slow_queries_per_min and replication_lag_ms could not be retrieved (backend 503 after retries); these might corroborate the WAL/consumer status but are not essential to the conclusion.
No telemetry for the analytics_cdc consumer service that owns the replication slot was found, so the reason the slot is inactive is unconfirmed.
No logs available from portfolio-service or settlement-service in the window (0 matches), so impact on those consumers of ledger-db is unverified.

findings.statement: Only one deployment in the window: payment-service v6.0.0 deployed 14:46 (new UPI mandate flow, ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD), rolled back at 15:12; no config/flag changes occurred.
ledger-db is a shared postgres used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
Prior incident HIST-114 (2025-04-18) on ledger-db had the same pattern: 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', resolved by dropping the slot.
